Its beginning to look a lot like Christmas

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
South Africans have had a tough year to say the least, but as we hurtle towards the festive season we bring you the story of Tannie Ida Strydom who will be bringing joy to our screens along side

Unique Selling Point:
... ahhh the sleepy town of Alberton in the East Rand...Many would say, "Nothing really happens they'', but as you walk the docile neighbourhood streets you might hear wonderful harmonic sounds emanating from somewhere.... of course is Tannie Ida and her girl's choir belting out Christmas carols in preparation for the festive season.

Tannie Idá is a bubbly 72-year-old who has an incredible passion for music that goes back to the dawn of democracy in the country she founded The Cantare Children’s Choir is one of South Africa’s young jewels. Not only is it known for its outstanding singing but it is one of the first and successful creations of the new diversity in South Africa.

The choir was founded in 1995 by Ida Strydom who has been the conductor to date. Her lifelong passion for choir music has firmly founded the character of the choir.Their singing and movements move the spectator with a keen desire to participate in their activity. Sitting still with a stern face would not be possible at all.

Apart from offering such world-class entertainment, the choir has a long list of accolades that makes each member proud to be called a Cantare singer.The choir has participated in the World Choir Games in 2004, 2006 and 2008 and brought home a fine selection of gold, silver and bronze medals. Other international competitions include the International Eisteddfod in Wales, the VII Advent and Christmas Festival in Bratislava as well as the Golden Voices of Montserrat Festival and Competition, Lloret de Mar, Spain. All these events yielded a rich harvest of gold and silver accolades.

On the local front, the choir was awarded the title of Outstanding Children’s Choir by the South African Choral Society. The choir has hosted international choirs visiting South Africa and they regularly appear on radio and television and other local festivals such as the Music of the Mountains Festival with the Drakensberg Boys Choir.



Summary:
The Christmas special will follow this order during the broadcast :
Part 1 : A two minute Musical Taser
Part 2: A four or five-minute insert on Ida and choir

Part 3 a four or five minute musical video with Ida and the choir

Extra Budget Items:
We might need a budget for the shoot location , possible venue hire for at Holy Trinity to record sound.

Script:


Script : Tannie Ida

1.V/O Alberton in Jo'burg may look peaceful, but over the years, we've uncovered a wild side—giraffes in unexpected predicaments and dodgy characters aplenty. It's not your average town!

[ transition flash]

Link Masa : But I am not here to track down an elusive scammer or confront a corrupt official, we have received word of mysterious sounds in this neighbourhood.

[bridging sounds in the background]

2.V/O Word on the street was that these… sounds often get louder as the festive season approaches…[stern tone] We were compelled to investigate …

[ Sequence Masa following the music all over the neighbourhood, playful investigative Pink Panther sort of music in the background]

3.V/O My search led me to this house…

4.V/O Turns out the perpetrator is a pensioner - Ida Strydom… fondly known as Tannie Eda … getting her award-winning choirready for a Christmas performance.


Upsound Masa07:09 How did your neighbours react when they heard the melodies coming out of this house?

Upsound Tannie Ida 07:09 I don't think they mind but they sometimes close their door.
[transition: choir singing]

5.V/O At 73, with a decorated career spanning three decades, Tannie Eda still has a jampacked schedule, as she’s regularly invited to judge choir competitions the world over. Retirement - not on her playlist!

Upsound Tannie 17:16 I think music, you can do that until you're old. I'm still singing as an old woman.
Upsound Masa But enjoying it and doing it well.
6.V/O It all started in 1997 when Eda left a teaching job to start a choir she hoped would reflect the changing times in the country… with a handful of eager children in her backyard, they started the Cantare Children’s Choir.
Upsound 10:24 society changed and Children need to be kept busy with positive things, that is my opinion.Our communities, previous disadvantaged people, they love singing. And that is what it's all about.
7.V/O Spotting musical talent in need of nurture, in 2003 she started development choirs in Tembisa, Katlehong and Thokoza - some of the city’s most under-resourced townships.
Upsound 26:02 Tannie Ida :That was a wonderful project to help establish these choirs. They all have their own conductors and their own little committees working with them. developing the children and we had lots of fun with them.
8.V/O: For her choir members Tannie Eda is much more than just a music teacher.
Upsound Zandile Msimanga 03:21 I am so grateful to Tannie Ida for introducing me to singing and having a place to go when I'm sad when I'm stressed. Yeah
Upsoundn Jeandri Auntie Ida taught me that if I don't have confidence in myself singing high notes, she just told me just throw it and do it, reach for the mountains. And that actually gave me confidence. She gave me confidence in believing that I can do it and I can sing. So it's not just only about teaching you how to sing.
9.V/O Her choir has excelled on a global stage.
Upsound Ida pictures: This looks impressive.We started off with the Choir Olympics in Bremen when we got a bronze medal.We got more experience. And then we went to China, and then we got a silver medal. And then we got to Graz,10:26 we got a gold medal
10.V/O keen to improve my own musical skills, I asked Tannie Eda for a few pointers.
Link 00:09 I'll admit I've had a few piano lessons in my lifetime, but never have I been taught by an award-winning conductor.
Upsound Lession 00:19What should I be doing? Okay, your sitting position is properly now, so that's nice. Put your hands on the piano. And always try to get this straight as it is now, and nice round fingers playing with the tippy of your fingers. So there you are. Nice short nails.
11.V/O So between, [ clears throat] impromptu music lessons, choir practice and developing the next big talent… This Tannie still makes time to pursue her own musical ambitions.
Upsound Tannie Ida : 17:46 I'm also in a trio that three ladies and we're not that young anymore but we love singing and we sing at concerts or in the churches especially in Christmas time we love our singing.
12. V/O Dedicated to the craft, and committed to enhancing the licall sheetves of others…for many Tannie Eda stands as a shining example of the true spirit of Christmas.
Upsound Ida 19:18 I'm just a normal person doing what I love. [ Masa] And what you love has changed so many people's lives.
[end]

Promos 3 x 21
—-Singing—
V/O : Christmas, the most wonderful time of the year and in this quiet suburb one Tannie is changing lives one music note at a time.
—- singing —
Upsound Zandile Msimanga 03:21 I am so grateful to Tannie Ida for introducing me to singing and having a place to go when I'm sad when I'm stressed.

Promo 2… 21 seconds
— Singing —
V/O It's the most wonderful time of the year, and in the suburb of Alberton, Johannesburg one Tannie is spreading the Christmas spirit with her award-winning choir.
Upsound 10:24 society changed and Children need to be kept busy with positive things, that is my opinion.Our communities, previous disadvantaged people, they love singing. And that is what it's all about.
— Singing






Promo 3 …21 seconds
—- Choir Singing—
V/O At 73 she is a decorated choir conductor with a voice match —
—- Tani Ida singing
V/O meet Tannie Ida and her award-winning choir, as they spread Christmas cheer- one note at a time.
